tableDescriptions.inventory.item__t: Individual physical or electronic item records (barcodes, status, call number, material type, loan type). Each item belongs to a holdings_record.
tableDescriptions.inventory.holdings_record__t: Holdings records linking instances to locations. Contains shelving info, call numbers, and location assignments.
tableDescriptions.inventory.instance__t: Bibliographic instance records (title, contributors, identifiers, publication info). The top-level catalog entity.
tableDescriptions.inventory.loccampus__t: Campus locations in the library consortium (e.g. Smith College, Amherst College, Hampshire College). Represents institutional campuses â€” NOT vendors or organizations.
tableDescriptions.inventory.locinstitution__t: Top-level institutional entities in the location hierarchy (e.g. Five Colleges consortium).
tableDescriptions.inventory.loclibrary__t: Library locations within a campus (e.g. Young Science Library, Neilson Library). Child of loccampus.
tableDescriptions.inventory.location__t: Specific shelving/storage locations within a library (e.g. Main Stacks, Reserve Desk). Lowest level of location hierarchy.
tableDescriptions.inventory.material_type__t: Material type definitions (book, DVD, serial, sound recording, microform, etc.).
tableDescriptions.inventory.loan_type__t: Loan type/circulation rule definitions (Can circulate, Course reserves, Non-circulating, etc.).
tableDescriptions.inventory.instance_type__t: Resource type definitions for instances (text, cartographic image, performed music, etc.).
tableDescriptions.inventory.instance_status__t: Cataloging status for instances (cataloged, uncataloged, batch loaded, etc.).
tableDescriptions.inventory.instance_format__t: Physical format of instances (volume, microfilm, online resource, etc.).
tableDescriptions.inventory.holdings_type__t: Holdings type definitions (physical, electronic, monograph, serial, multi-part monograph).
tableDescriptions.inventory.call_number_type__t: Call number classification schemes (Library of Congress, Dewey Decimal, SuDoc, NLM, etc.).
tableDescriptions.inventory.service_point__t: Service desks/points where circulation transactions occur (e.g. Circ Desk, ILL Office).
tableDescriptions.inventory.classification_type__t: Classification system types used for instance classification (LC, Dewey, etc.).
tableDescriptions.inventory.contributor_name_type__t: Types of contributor names (personal, corporate, meeting).
tableDescriptions.inventory.contributor_type__t: Contributor role types (author, editor, illustrator, etc.).
tableDescriptions.inventory.identifier_type__t: Identifier type definitions (ISBN, ISSN, OCLC, LCCN, etc.).
tableDescriptions.inventory.statistical_code__t: Statistical code values used for item/holdings/instance categorization and reporting.
tableDescriptions.inventory.statistical_code_type__t: Statistical code type definitions (ARL, DISC, etc.).
tableDescriptions.inventory.alternative_title_type__t: Types of alternative titles (uniform title, variant title, etc.).
tableDescriptions.inventory.electronic_access_relationship: Types of electronic access relationships (resource, version of resource, related resource, etc.).
tableDescriptions.inventory.mode_of_issuance__t: Mode of issuance for instances (single unit, multipart monograph, serial, integrating resource).
tableDescriptions.inventory.nature_of_content_term__t: Nature of content terms (autobiography, bibliography, catalog, etc.).
tableDescriptions.inventory.holdings_note_type__t: Types of notes that can be attached to holdings records.
tableDescriptions.inventory.item_note_type__t: Types of notes that can be attached to item records.
tableDescriptions.inventory.ill_policy__t: Interlibrary loan policy definitions for holdings.
tableDescriptions.inventory.instance_note_type__t: Types of notes for instance records.
tableDescriptions.inventory.instance_relationship_type__t: Types of relationships between instances (bound-with, analytics, etc.).
tableDescriptions.circulation.loan__t: Current state of item loans â€” each loan has ONE row showing its LATEST state. Use ONLY for queries about what is currently checked out right now (WHERE action = 'checkedout'). Do NOT use for counting historical checkouts, returns, or renewals â€” use circulation.audit_loan__t instead.
tableDescriptions.circulation.loan_policy__t: Loan policy definitions (loan period, renewals allowed, grace period, etc.).
tableDescriptions.circulation.fixed_due_date_schedule__t: Fixed due date schedule definitions for loan policies.

tableDescriptions.circulation.user_request_preference__t: Patron preferences for request fulfillment (delivery, hold shelf).
tableDescriptions.orders.po_line__t: Purchase order lines â€” individual line items on purchase orders. Contains material type, cost, fund, physical/electronic details.

vocabulary.college: inventory.loccampus__t.name â€” campuses in the consortium (Smith College, Amherst College, etc.). NOT organizations.
vocabulary.campus: inventory.loccampus__t.name â€” campuses in the location hierarchy.
vocabulary.institution: inventory.locinstitution__t.name â€” top-level institution (e.g. Five Colleges consortium).
vocabulary.library: inventory.loclibrary__t.name â€” libraries within a campus (e.g. Neilson Library, Young Science Library).
vocabulary.location: inventory.location__t.name â€” specific shelving locations within a library (e.g. Main Stacks, Reserve).
vocabulary.effective location: inventory.item__t.effective_location_id â€” ALWAYS use this for location joins on items, NOT permanent_location_id. The effective location reflects temporary/current location overrides.
vocabulary.item location: inventory.item__t.effective_location_id â€” join to inventory.location__t.id. NEVER use holdings_record__t.permanent_location_id for circulation or item-level queries.
vocabulary.vendor: organizations.organizations__t.name â€” vendors/suppliers you purchase materials from (EBSCO, GOBI, YBP).
vocabulary.publisher: inventory.instance__t.index_title or publication fields â€” NOT organizations.
vocabulary.patron: users.users__t â€” user/patron records. Join to users.groups__t for patron group.
vocabulary.student: users.users__t joined to users.groups__t where group = student type.
vocabulary.faculty: users.users__t joined to users.groups__t where group = 'Faculty'.
vocabulary.checkout: circulation.audit_loan__t â€” use for counting checkouts. Each checkout is a separate row. Filter with: loan__action IN ('checkedout', 'checkedOutThroughOverride'). Join items via loan__item_id. loan_date is loan__loan_date. Do NOT use circulation.loan__t for counting checkouts â€” it only stores the current state of each loan.
vocabulary.loan: circulation.audit_loan__t â€” the audit log of all loan events. Use for counting loan activity. Columns use the loan__ prefix: loan__item_id, loan__action, loan__loan_date, loan__due_date, loan__return_date. Use circulation.loan__t ONLY for current-state queries (e.g. what is currently checked out right now).
vocabulary.checkin: circulation.audit_loan__t where loan__action = 'checkedin' â€” for counting checkins. Or circulation.check_in__t for check-in transaction records. Do NOT use circulation.loan__t.return_date for counting returns â€” loan__t only shows the current state.
vocabulary.return: circulation.audit_loan__t where loan__action = 'checkedin' â€” for counting returns. The loan__return_date column contains the return timestamp. Do NOT use circulation.loan__t.return_date for counting â€” use audit_loan__t.
vocabulary.overdue: circulation.loan__t where due_date < CURRENT_DATE AND return_date IS NULL â€” active overdue loans.
vocabulary.fine: feesfines.accounts__t â€” fee/fine charges on patron accounts.
vocabulary.purchased: orders.po_line__t â€” purchase order lines. Use purchase_order__t.date_ordered for purchase date.
vocabulary.ordered: orders.purchase_order__t.date_ordered â€” the date a purchase order was placed.
vocabulary.material type: inventory.material_type__t.name â€” type of material (Book, DVD, serial, etc.). Values are Title Case in the database â€” always use ILIKE or LOWER() for matching.
vocabulary.format: inventory.instance_format__t.name â€” physical format of an instance.
vocabulary.barcode: inventory.item__t.barcode â€” item barcode, or users.users__t.barcode â€” patron barcode.
vocabulary.title: inventory.instance__t.title â€” bibliographic title.
vocabulary.budget: finance.budget__t â€” budget allocations per fund per fiscal year.
vocabulary.invoice: invoice.invoices__t â€” vendor invoices. Use invoice_lines__t for line items.
vocabulary.fiscal year: finance.fiscal_year__t.name or .code â€” fiscal year definition.
vocabulary.expense class: finance.expense_class__t.name â€” spending category (Electronic, Print, etc.).
vocabulary.service point: inventory.service_point__t.name â€” circulation desk / service location.
vocabulary.patron group: users.groups__t.group â€” patron type (Faculty, Undergraduate, Graduate, Staff).
vocabulary.circulation log: audit.circulation_logs__t â€” audit trail of circulation events.
vocabulary.circulating: circulation.audit_loan__t â€” count loan events to measure circulation. Filter with loan__action IN ('checkedout', 'checkedOutThroughOverride'). Join loan__item_id â†’ inventory.item__t â†’ effective_location_id â†’ location__t â†’ loclibrary__t â†’ loccampus__t for location context.
vocabulary.book: inventory.material_type__t where LOWER(name) = 'book'. The database stores 'Book' (capitalized). Always use case-insensitive comparison.
vocabulary.equipment: inventory.material_type__t where LOWER(name) LIKE '%equipment%'. Exclude with AND LOWER(imt.name) NOT LIKE '%equipment%'.
vocabulary.anonymized data: User/patron records (users.users__t) are ANONYMIZED. NEVER use patron data (custom_fields, patron group joins, user campus fields) to determine which campus or institution a borrower belongs to. Instead, use checkout_service_point_id and checkin_service_point_id on circulation.loan__t as proxies for where transactions happened. Match service point IDs to known campus service points to identify cross-campus activity.
vocabulary.consortial circulation: To identify cross-campus lending/borrowing in the Five Colleges consortium, use this approach: (1) Item ownership = item_effective_location_id_at_check_out -> inventory.location__t.campus_id (Smith campus IDs: '7d02e46d-3e60-4eaf-a986-5aa3550e8cb5' for Smith College, 'b23a14ae-b3a8-4cbf-92fb-4b81d1a4b0a1' for Repository). (2) Transaction location = checkout_service_point_id / checkin_service_point_id matched against known campus service points. (3) Lending out = Smith-owned items checked out at NON-Smith service points. (4) Borrowing in = non-Smith-owned items checked out at Smith service points. NEVER use users.users__t joins â€” data is anonymized.
vocabulary.consortial lending: Same as 'consortial circulation'. Lending out = Smith-owned items (campus_at_co in Smith/Repository campus IDs) where checkout_service_point_id is NOT a Smith service point. Use service points as proxy â€” NOT user/patron data (anonymized).
vocabulary.consortial borrowing: Same as 'consortial circulation'. Borrowing in = non-Smith-owned items (campus_at_co NOT in Smith/Repository campus IDs) where checkout_service_point_id IS a Smith service point. Use service points as proxy â€” NOT user/patron data (anonymized).
vocabulary.Smith College service points: Smith College service point UUIDs for identifying transactions at Smith: '2c0764b7-63b3-4254-9950-0c730b7e438b' (SC Neilson Library), '6b6b9f00-aac7-4e20-a819-fb24386e48bb' (SC Self Check), '25d98f21-ef4d-4846-955e-17840062b1f0' (SC Hillyer Art Library), '602aba21-73ae-4e43-a92e-91f2dee34c8f' (SC Josten Library), '9e4b06c8-0cb0-4011-ab1d-a23af57d190c' (SC Annex). Use with checkout_service_point_id / checkin_service_point_id on circulation.loan__t.
vocabulary.Smith College campus IDs: Smith College campus UUIDs in inventory.loccampus__t for determining item ownership via item_effective_location_id_at_check_out -> location.campus_id: '7d02e46d-3e60-4eaf-a986-5aa3550e8cb5' (Smith College campus), 'b23a14ae-b3a8-4cbf-92fb-4b81d1a4b0a1' (Repository campus â€” also Smith-owned). Both should be included when identifying Smith-owned items.
vocabulary.renewal: circulation.audit_loan__t where loan__action = 'renewed' â€” each renewal is a separate row in the audit table. Do NOT use loan__t.renewal_count to count renewals â€” in FOLIO initial checkouts have renewal_count = 0, not NULL, making it unreliable for filtering.
vocabulary.physical materials: When filtering for physical/tangible materials (excluding equipment and e-resources), use this list of material_type__t.name values: 'Book', 'Journal', 'Serial', 'Newspaper', 'Score', 'Thesis/Dissertation', 'Government Publication', 'Microform', 'DVD/Blu-ray', 'Audio CD', 'CD-ROM', 'Videocassette', 'LP Phonorecord', 'Audiocassette', 'Film'. Build as a CTE with unnest(array[...]) for clean filtering.
vocabulary.campus abbreviation SC: SC = Smith College. Library and location names prefixed with SC belong to Smith College (e.g. SC Neilson Library, SC Hillyer Art Library).
vocabulary.campus abbreviation AC: AC = Amherst College. Library and location names prefixed with AC belong to Amherst College (e.g. AC Frost Library, AC Science Library).
vocabulary.campus abbreviation MH: MH = Mount Holyoke College. Library and location names prefixed with MH belong to Mount Holyoke College (e.g. MH Main Library).
vocabulary.campus abbreviation UM: UM = University Of Massachusetts. Library and location names prefixed with UM belong to UMass (e.g. UM W.E.B. Du Bois Library).
vocabulary.campus abbreviation HC: HC = Hampshire College. Library and location names prefixed with HC belong to Hampshire College (e.g. HC Harold Johnson Library).
vocabulary.campus abbreviation RP: RP = Five Colleges Collections. Library and location names prefixed with RP belong to the shared Five Colleges repository.
vocabulary.campus abbreviation YB: YB = National Yiddish Book Center. Library and location names prefixed with YB belong to the Yiddish Book Center.
vocabulary.location naming convention: In this Five Colleges FOLIO instance, ALL library names and location names are prefixed with a 2-letter campus abbreviation code (SC, AC, MH, UM, HC, RP, YB). When searching for a library or location by name, use ILIKE with a wildcard pattern to match regardless of prefix, e.g. WHERE name ILIKE '%Neilson%' instead of exact match.
vocabulary.academic year: When a user says 'current year', 'this year', or 'academic year', they mean the academic/fiscal year running July 1 through June 30. Never assume calendar year (Jan-Dec) unless the user explicitly says 'calendar year'. To calculate the current academic year dynamically, ALWAYS use a CTE with the WITH keyword: WITH academic_year_dates AS ( SELECT CASE WHEN CURRENT_DATE >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE) + INTERVAL '6 months' THEN date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE) + INTERVAL '6 months' ELSE date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE) - INTERVAL '6 months' END AS start_date, CASE WHEN CURRENT_DATE >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE) + INTERVAL '6 months' THEN date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE) + INTERVAL '1 year' + INTERVAL '6 months' - INTERVAL '1 day' ELSE date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE) + INTERVAL '6 months' - INTERVAL '1 day' END AS end_date ) â€” then reference it with: JOIN academic_year_dates ayd ON TRUE and filter with: WHERE date_column >= ayd.start_date AND date_column <= ayd.end_date. CRITICAL: The WITH keyword and CTE name 'academic_year_dates AS (' must appear at the start of the query. If the query has other CTEs, chain them with commas after the academic_year_dates CTE.
vocabulary.circulation data: Circulation data comes from THREE sources: (1) circulation.audit_loan__t â€” the AUDIT LOG of all loan events (~2.2M rows). Use this for COUNTING checkouts. Each checkout/checkin/renewal is a separate row. Columns use the loan__ prefix: loan__item_id, loan__action, loan__loan_date, loan__due_date, loan__return_date. Filter checkouts with: loan__action IN ('checkedout', 'checkedOutThroughOverride'). Group by loan__item_id. (2) circulation.loan__t â€” the CURRENT STATE of each loan (~677K rows). Each loan has ONE row showing its latest state. The action column shows the LAST action (e.g. 'checkedin' for returned books). Use this ONLY for "what is currently checked out" queries (WHERE action = 'checkedout'). Do NOT use loan__t for counting historical checkouts â€” a returned book has action='checkedin', not 'checkedout'. Columns have NO prefix: item_id, action, loan_date. (3) Historic/former circulation from the ALEPH system (migrated in 2022), stored in inventory.item__t__notes where notes__item_note_type_id = 'f765f19f-9f1c-4688-8c79-ec366a730842'. The note value is a plain text number extracted with CAST(COALESCE(NULLIF(REGEXP_REPLACE(notes__note, '\D', '', 'g'), ''), '0') AS INTEGER). Join historic data to items via hrid. When the user asks for TOTAL, LIFETIME, ALL-TIME, or CUMULATIVE circulation, include audit_loan__t checkouts + former circulation notes. When the user asks for circulation within a specific TIME PERIOD (e.g. 'this year', 'last 30 days'), use ONLY audit_loan__t with date filters. NEVER use renewal_count IS NULL â€” it is unreliable. The action filter alone is sufficient.
vocabulary.former circulation: "Former circulation", "historic circulation", or "ALEPH circulation", "Cumulative circulation", "Total Circulation" refers to cumulative checkout counts migrated from the ALEPH ILS into FOLIO item notes. Located in inventory.item__t__notes where notes__item_note_type_id = 'f765f19f-9f1c-4688-8c79-ec366a730842'. The note contains a plain-text number. Extract it with: CAST(COALESCE(NULLIF(REGEXP_REPLACE(notes__note, '\D', '', 'g'), ''), '0') AS INTEGER). Join to item__t on hrid. Always LEFT JOIN since not all items have historic data.
vocabulary.Current year: current data only â€” ignore inventory.item__t__notes with former circulation
vocabulary.All time / historical / everything: include notes â€” combine circulation.loan__t + former circulation notes
vocabulary.Ask for clarification: if the request is ambiguous (e.g., "top circulating books" without a time qualifier)
vocabulary.query performance optimization: CRITICAL PERFORMANCE AND CORRECTNESS RULES: (1) Use circulation.audit_loan__t for counting checkouts â€” it has one row per loan EVENT. Filter with loan__action IN ('checkedout', 'checkedOutThroughOverride'). Columns use the loan__ prefix: loan__item_id, loan__action, loan__loan_date. (2) Do NOT use circulation.loan__t for counting checkouts â€” it stores the CURRENT STATE of each loan. A returned book has action='checkedin', so filtering action='checkedout' misses all returned items. Only use loan__t for "what is currently checked out right now" queries. (3) When a query uses CTEs (WITH clauses) that aggregate large tables, ALWAYS define a target_items CTE FIRST that applies all WHERE filters (location, campus, material type, etc.), then JOIN the circulation/notes CTEs to target_items. BAD pattern (timeout): CTE aggregates ALL rows, outer query filters. GOOD pattern (fast): target_items CTE with filters first, then circulation CTE joins to target_items. (4) NEVER use renewal_count IS NULL to filter initial checkouts â€” in FOLIO, initial checkouts have renewal_count = 0, not NULL. The loan__action filter alone is sufficient to identify checkouts.
vocabulary.call number ranges:
When grouping or counting by call number range or classification, NEVER use LEFT(call_number, 1) as a range â€” this incorrectly groups all LC classes starting with H (H, HA, HB, HC, HF, HQ, etc.) into one bucket and completely mishandles Dewey numbers.

Use this CASE expression to extract call number class correctly:

CASE
    -- LC Call Number: extract the leading letter(s) only (1-3 letters before the first digit)
    WHEN effective_call_number_components__call_number ~ '^[A-Z]{1,3}[0-9]'
    THEN REGEXP_REPLACE(effective_call_number_components__call_number, '^([A-Z]{1,3})[0-9].*', '\1')
    -- Dewey Call Number: extract the 3-digit hundred class (e.g. 823.914 â†’ 800)
    WHEN effective_call_number_components__call_number ~ '^[0-9]'
    THEN LPAD(
            CAST(
                FLOOR(CAST(REGEXP_REPLACE(effective_call_number_components__call_number, '^([0-9]+).*', '\1') AS NUMERIC) / 100) * 100
            AS TEXT),
         3, '0')
    ELSE 'Unknown'
END AS call_number_class

LC examples:
  'H 123'    â†’ 'H'
  'HA 456'   â†’ 'HA'
  'HF 1234'  â†’ 'HF'
  'QA 76'    â†’ 'QA'
  'PS 3561'  â†’ 'PS'

Dewey examples:
  '823.914'  â†’ '800'
  '153.4'    â†’ '100'
  '372.6'    â†’ '300'

When asked for "call number range" or "call number prefix" or "classification", apply this CASE expression. When asked for a broader grouping (LC subclass description like "H = Social Sciences"), also provide a label by JOINing or CASE-matching the extracted class against known LC class descriptions.

When a user asks which call number RANGES have the highest circulation, use this expression in the GROUP BY and SELECT. Do NOT use LEFT(..., 1) or SUBSTRING(..., 1, 1).
vocabulary.library grouping:
When a user lists multiple libraries (e.g. "for Neilson, Josten, and Hillyer") or says "from each library" or "by library", ALWAYS include the library name in SELECT and GROUP BY to show individual counts per library. This is the DEFAULT behavior â€” show one row per library.

Only combine libraries into a single total when the user explicitly says "total", "combined", "altogether", "sum across", or "how many total".

Examples of INDIVIDUAL counts (GROUP BY lib.name):
- "circulation for Neilson, Josten and Hillyer" â†’ one row per library
- "from each of the three libraries" â†’ one row per library
- "for individual counts from Neilson and Hillyer" â†’ one row per library
- "checkouts at Neilson and Josten" â†’ one row per library
- "how many items at each library" â†’ one row per library

Examples of COMBINED total (no GROUP BY lib.name, or SUM across):
- "total circulation across Neilson, Josten and Hillyer" â†’ single number
- "combined checkouts from all three libraries" â†’ single number
- "how many altogether from Neilson and Josten" â†’ single number

When in doubt, default to individual counts per library.
vocabulary.MARC record: MARC bibliographic data is stored in folio_source_record.records__t.parsed_record__content as a TEXT column (NOT JSONB). It contains a JSON string representation of the MARC record. To check if a MARC field exists (e.g. field 300), use: parsed_record__content ILIKE '%"300"%'. To check if a field does NOT exist: parsed_record__content NOT ILIKE '%"300"%'. To search for a specific subfield value: parsed_record__content ILIKE '%"650"%somevalue%'. NEVER use jsonb_exists(), jsonb_path_query(), ->> operator, or any JSONB functions on this column â€” it is TEXT. NEVER cast it to JSONB â€” the content is too large and the cast will timeout. Always use ILIKE/NOT ILIKE pattern matching for MARC field queries. Join to instances via: folio_source_record.records__t.external_ids_holder__instance_id = inventory.instance__t.id.
vocabulary.marctab_join_safety: CRITICAL: marctab.mtNNN tables have instance_id as UUID type but inventory.instance__t.id may be TEXT type. Joining on these columns causes ERROR: operator does not exist: uuid = text. ALWAYS join on instance_hrid instead: marctab.mtNNN.instance_hrid = inventory.instance__t.hrid (both text, safe to compare). This applies to ALL marctab tables (mt000â€“mt999).
vocabulary.marctab per-field table structure:
The marctab schema contains one table per MARC field: marctab.mt000 through marctab.mt999. Each table contains ONLY rows for that MARC tag.

Columns per table: srs_id (UUID), instance_hrid (text, links to inventory.instance__t.hrid), instance_id (UUID), field (tag, e.g. '300'), ind1, ind2, ord (occurrence number for repeated fields), sf_a, sf_b, sf_c, sf_d, sf_e, sf_f, sf_g, sf_h, sf_i, sf_j, sf_k, sf_l, sf_m, sf_n, sf_o, sf_p, sf_q, sf_r, sf_s, sf_t, sf_u, sf_v, sf_w, sf_x, sf_y, sf_z, sf_0, sf_1, sf_2, sf_3, sf_4, sf_5, sf_6, sf_7, sf_8, sf_9.

Subfields are COLUMNS (not rows). To get the 245$a title: SELECT m.sf_a FROM marctab.mt245 m WHERE m.instance_hrid = inst.hrid.

NEVER use folio_source_record.marctab (the VIEW) â€” it unions all ~1000 tables and causes 668K+ cost even with filters. Always use the specific marctab.mtNNN table for the field you need.

  marctab.mt001 â€” control number

  marctab.mt260 â€” publication (old format: sf_a = place, sf_b = publisher, sf_c = date)
  marctab.mt264 â€” publication (sf_a = place, sf_b = publisher, sf_c = date)
  marctab.mt300 â€” physical description (sf_a = extent, sf_b = other details, sf_c = dimensions)
  marctab.mt490 â€” series statement

  marctab.mt504 â€” bibliography note

Always query the SPECIFIC marctab.mtNNN table, never all 1000.
vocabulary.item__t index awareness:
CRITICAL: inventory.item__t benefits from a composite index on (holdings_record_id, material_type_id). Create it with:

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_item_holdings_material
ON inventory.item__t (holdings_record_id, material_type_id);

When querying items by holdings or material type, ALWAYS structure queries to take advantage of this index:
- Drive from holdings â†’ items using holdings_record_id (index leading column)
- Filter by material_type_id in the same lookup (index second column)
- Use nested EXISTS (not JOIN + DISTINCT) so PostgreSQL can do index-only semi-join probes
- NEVER scan item__t first and then join back to holdings â€” that forces a 10M+ row seq scan

CAVEAT: LDP/MetaDB rebuilds tables nightly. If the index is dropped during refresh, re-create it via a post-refresh script or cron job.

The ONLY default indexes on item__t are:
- item__t_id_idx (id)
- item__t___id_idx (__id)

Without idx_item_holdings_material, any EXISTS or JOIN through holdings_record_id does a full sequential scan.
vocabulary.nested EXISTS pattern for instance-level:
CRITICAL PERFORMANCE RULE: When building instance-level result sets with item-level filters (material type, item status, etc.), ALWAYS use nested EXISTS with MATERIALIZED CTEs. Never use JOIN + DISTINCT.

PATTERN:
WITH result AS MATERIALIZED (
    SELECT inst.id, inst.hrid, inst.title
    FROM inventory.instance__t inst
    WHERE EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
        FROM inventory.holdings_record__t hr
        WHERE hr.instance_id = inst.id
          AND [any holdings-level filters]
          AND EXISTS (
              SELECT 1
              FROM inventory.item__t ii
              WHERE ii.holdings_record_id = hr.id
                AND [any item-level filters like material_type_id]
          )
    )
)

This pattern:
1. Uses the index on holdings_record__t(instance_id) to find holdings for each instance
2. Uses the composite index idx_item_holdings_material on item__t(holdings_record_id, material_type_id) to check items
3. EXISTS is a semi-join â€” stops at first match per instance
4. MATERIALIZED prevents the planner from inlining the CTE and making bad join order decisions

For material type filtering, resolve the material_type_id with a scalar subquery:
  ii.material_type_id = (SELECT id FROM inventory.material_type__t WHERE LOWER(name) = 'book' LIMIT 1)

This avoids joining the material_type__t table into the main query, which can confuse the planner.
vocabulary.MARC source record access:
When a user requests MARC record data, use the appropriate approach:

1. FIELD-LEVEL queries (check existence, extract subfield, filter by value): Use marctab.mtNNN per-field tables. Example: marctab.mt300 for physical description, marctab.mt245 for title.
   SELECT m.sf_a FROM marctab.mt245 m WHERE m.instance_hrid = inst.hrid

2. FULL MARC record output (raw source, complete MARC, export): Use folio_source_record.records__t.parsed_record__content.
   JOIN folio_source_record.records__t sr ON sr.external_id = inst.id AND sr.state = 'ACTUAL'

NEVER use the folio_source_record.marctab VIEW â€” it unions ~1000 tables and causes 668K+ query cost. Always use marctab.mtNNN directly.

Use records__t.parsed_record__content when the user wants: the full/complete MARC record, raw source record, MARC data for export.
Use marctab.mtNNN when the user wants: to check if a field exists, filter by a subfield value, extract specific subfields.
vocabulary.CTE MATERIALIZED keyword:
ALWAYS use AS MATERIALIZED for CTEs that scope instances by campus, location, or any multi-table filter chain. Without MATERIALIZED, PostgreSQL 12+ may inline the CTE and make catastrophic join order decisions on large tables.

Example:
WITH sc_instances AS MATERIALIZED (
    SELECT inst.id, inst.hrid, inst.title
    FROM inventory.instance__t inst
    WHERE EXISTS (...)
)

This forces PostgreSQL to:
1. Execute the CTE first and store results in memory/temp
2. Use accurate row counts for subsequent query planning
3. Prevent the optimizer from flattening CTEs into joins that trigger full seq scans on 10M+ row tables
vocabulary.MARC data:
When a user asks about MARC fields or MARC records, use marctab.mtNNN per-field tables (e.g. marctab.mt245 for title, marctab.mt300 for physical description). Each table has subfields as COLUMNS: sf_a, sf_b, sf_c, etc.

To show MARC subfield data:
  SELECT m.instance_hrid, m.sf_a, m.sf_b, m.sf_c
  FROM marctab.mt300 m
  WHERE m.instance_hrid IN (SELECT hrid FROM <filtered_set>)
  ORDER BY m.instance_hrid, m.ord

To show multiple MARC fields, JOIN multiple mtNNN tables:
  LEFT JOIN marctab.mt245 m245 ON m245.instance_hrid = sbi.hrid
  LEFT JOIN marctab.mt300 m300 ON m300.instance_hrid = sbi.hrid

NEVER use folio_source_record.marctab (the VIEW) â€” it unions ~1000 underlying tables and causes 668K+ query cost.

When a user says "show me the MARC record" or "expand the MARC data", either:
  (a) JOIN the specific marctab.mtNNN tables for the fields they care about, OR
  (b) Use folio_source_record.records__t.parsed_record__content for the complete raw MARC JSON.
vocabulary.MARC field:
A specific MARC tag number (e.g. 245, 300, 650). Use the corresponding marctab.mtNNN table:
  marctab.mt245 for field 245, marctab.mt300 for field 300, marctab.mt650 for field 650, etc.

Subfields are COLUMNS in each table: sf_a, sf_b, sf_c, ... sf_z, sf_0 ... sf_9.
  Example: SELECT m.sf_a FROM marctab.mt245 m WHERE m.instance_hrid = inst.hrid

ord column distinguishes repeated fields (e.g. first 650 has ord=1, second has ord=2).

To check if a MARC field EXISTS:
  WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM marctab.mt300 m WHERE m.instance_hrid = inst.hrid)

To check if a MARC field DOES NOT EXIST:
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM marctab.mt300 m WHERE m.instance_hrid = inst.hrid)

NEVER use folio_source_record.marctab WHERE field = 'NNN' â€” the VIEW unions ~1000 tables (668K cost). Use marctab.mtNNN directly.
vocabulary.marctab:
MARC data is accessed via the marctab schema, which has one table per MARC field: marctab.mt000 through marctab.mt999.

Each table has columns: srs_id, instance_hrid, instance_id, field, ind1, ind2, ord, sf_a through sf_z, sf_0 through sf_9.

Subfields are COLUMNS (not rows): use m.sf_a, m.sf_b, etc.

Join to inventory via: marctab.mtNNN.instance_hrid = inventory.instance__t.hrid

WARNING: There is also a VIEW called folio_source_record.marctab that unions all ~1000 tables into (field, sf, content) rows. NEVER use this VIEW â€” it causes 668K+ query cost. Always use the specific marctab.mtNNN table for the field you need.

Examples:
  - Check field 300 exists: EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM marctab.mt300 m WHERE m.instance_hrid = inst.hrid)
  - Get ISBN: SELECT m.sf_a FROM marctab.mt020 m WHERE m.instance_hrid = inst.hrid
  - Get title: SELECT m.sf_a, m.sf_b FROM marctab.mt245 m WHERE m.instance_hrid = inst.hrid
vocabulary.MARC query with item filter performance:
When a MARC query also filters by item-level attributes (material type, item status, location), the TWO biggest performance factors are:

1. idx_item_holdings_material index on inventory.item__t(holdings_record_id, material_type_id) â€” turns each nested EXISTS probe from a 10M-row seq scan into an index seek. Without this index, the item__t EXISTS check alone can take minutes.

2. AS MATERIALIZED on the instance-scoping CTE â€” prevents PostgreSQL from inlining the CTE and making bad join-order decisions against the marctab view.

Both are required for sub-second performance on queries like "Smith College books missing MARC field 300". If the query times out, check that the composite index exists:
  SELECT indexname FROM pg_indexes WHERE tablename = 'item__t' AND indexdef LIKE '%holdings_record_id%material_type_id%';

If missing, create it:
  CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_item_holdings_material ON inventory.item__t (holdings_record_id, material_type_id);
vocabulary.marctab performance rule:
CRITICAL PERFORMANCE RULE for MARC queries:

1. ALWAYS use marctab.mtNNN per-field tables (e.g. marctab.mt300, marctab.mt245).
   Each table contains ONLY rows for that MARC tag, with an index on instance_hrid.
   Cost: single index seek per instance.

2. NEVER use folio_source_record.marctab (the VIEW).
   The VIEW is a UNION ALL of ~1000 marctab.mtNNN tables.
   Even with WHERE field = '300' and a scoped CTE, PostgreSQL cannot push the
   field predicate down into the union â€” it scans ALL 1000 tables.
   Cost: 668K+ regardless of filters.

3. For queries needing multiple MARC fields, use separate JOINs to each mtNNN table:
   LEFT JOIN marctab.mt245 m245 ON m245.instance_hrid = sbi.hrid
   LEFT JOIN marctab.mt300 m300 ON m300.instance_hrid = sbi.hrid
   LEFT JOIN marctab.mt650 m650 ON m650.instance_hrid = sbi.hrid

4. For complete raw MARC output, use folio_source_record.records__t.parsed_record__content
   (the JSON text column), NOT the marctab VIEW.

5. Combine with MATERIALIZED CTEs and nested EXISTS for instance scoping
   (see hints 190, 192).

examples.question: Show me all materials purchased in the last 90 days grouped by material type purchased by Smith College
examples.sql: SELECT imt.name AS material_type_name, SUM(COALESCE(pol.cost__quantity_physical, 1)) AS total_purchased FROM orders.po_line__t AS pol JOIN orders.purchase_order__t AS po ON pol.purchase_order_id = po.id JOIN inventory.material_type__t AS imt ON pol.physical__material_type = imt.id JOIN inventory.location__t AS loc ON pol.physical__expected_receipt_date IS NOT NULL JOIN inventory.loclibrary__t AS lib ON loc.library_id = lib.id JOIN inventory.loccampus__t AS camp ON lib.campus_id = camp.id WHERE camp.name = 'Smith College' AND po.date_ordered::date >= (CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '90 days') GROUP BY imt.name ORDER BY total_purchased DESC;

examples.question: How many items does each library have?
examples.sql: SELECT lib.name AS library_name, COUNT(ii.id) AS item_count FROM inventory.item__t AS ii JOIN inventory.location__t AS loc ON ii.effective_location_id = loc.id JOIN inventory.loclibrary__t AS lib ON loc.library_id = lib.id GROUP BY lib.name ORDER BY item_count DESC;

examples.question: What vendors have we spent the most money with this fiscal year?
examples.sql: SELECT org.name AS vendor_name, SUM(inv.total) AS total_spent FROM invoice.invoices__t AS inv JOIN organizations.organizations__t AS org ON inv.vendor_id = org.id WHERE inv.status = 'Paid' AND inv.invoice_date >= (SELECT start_date FROM finance.fiscal_year__t WHERE code = 'FY2026') GROUP BY org.name ORDER BY total_spent DESC LIMIT 20;

examples.question: Count checkouts by patron group for the Neilson Library in the last 30 days
examples.sql: SELECT ug.group AS patron_group, COUNT(al.id) AS checkout_count FROM circulation.audit_loan__t AS al JOIN inventory.item__t AS ii ON al.loan__item_id = ii.id JOIN users.users__t AS uu ON al.loan__user_id = uu.id JOIN users.groups__t AS ug ON uu.patron_group = ug.id JOIN inventory.location__t AS loc ON ii.effective_location_id = loc.id JOIN inventory.loclibrary__t AS lib ON loc.library_id = lib.id WHERE LOWER(lib.name) ILIKE '%Neilson%' AND al.loan__action IN ('checkedout', 'checkedOutThroughOverride') AND al.loan__loan_date >= (CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '30 days') GROUP BY ug.group ORDER BY checkout_count DESC;

examples.question: Show me the top 10 highest circulating books from Smith College between June 2024 and June 2025
examples.sql: SELECT lib.name AS library_name, ii.effective_call_number_components__call_number AS call_number, inst.title, MAX(al.loan__loan_date) AS last_circulation_date, COUNT(al.id) AS circulation_count FROM circulation.audit_loan__t AS al JOIN inventory.item__t AS ii ON al.loan__item_id = ii.id JOIN inventory.material_type__t AS imt ON ii.material_type_id = imt.id JOIN inventory.holdings_record__t AS hr ON ii.holdings_record_id = hr.id JOIN inventory.instance__t AS inst ON hr.instance_id = inst.id JOIN inventory.location__t AS loc ON ii.effective_location_id = loc.id JOIN inventory.loclibrary__t AS lib ON loc.library_id = lib.id JOIN inventory.loccampus__t AS camp ON lib.campus_id = camp.id WHERE al.loan__action IN ('checkedout', 'checkedOutThroughOverride') AND al.loan__loan_date::date >= '2024-06-30' AND al.loan__loan_date::date <= '2025-06-30' AND LOWER(camp.name) = LOWER('Smith College') AND LOWER(imt.name) = 'book' AND LOWER(imt.name) NOT LIKE '%equipment%' GROUP BY lib.name, ii.effective_call_number_components__call_number, inst.title ORDER BY circulation_count DESC LIMIT 10;

examples.question: Show me the number of items that have circulated from Smith College to another Five College member. Only show me July 1st, 2024 to June 30th, 2025. I do not want to see items circulated to Smith College patrons only to other members within the Five Colleges.
examples.sql:
WITH smith_sp AS (
  SELECT unnest(array[
    '2c0764b7-63b3-4254-9950-0c730b7e438b',
    '6b6b9f00-aac7-4e20-a819-fb24386e48bb',
    '25d98f21-ef4d-4846-955e-17840062b1f0',
    '602aba21-73ae-4e43-a92e-91f2dee34c8f',
    '9e4b06c8-0cb0-4011-ab1d-a23af57d190c'
  ])::text AS id
),
keep_materials AS (
  SELECT unnest(array[
    'Book','Journal','Serial','Newspaper','Score',
    'Thesis/Dissertation','Government Publication','Microform',
    'DVD/Blu-ray','Audio CD','CD-ROM','Videocassette',
    'LP Phonorecord','Audiocassette','Film'
  ]) AS name
),
base AS (
  SELECT l.id, l.checkout_service_point_id AS co_sp,
    l.checkin_service_point_id AS ci_sp,
    loc.campus_id AS campus_at_co, mt.name AS mtype
  FROM circulation.loan__t l
  JOIN inventory.location__t loc ON loc.id = l.item_effective_location_id_at_check_out
  JOIN inventory.item__t it ON it.id = l.item_id
  JOIN inventory.material_type__t mt ON mt.id = it.material_type_id
  WHERE l.loan_date::timestamptz >= '2024-07-01'
    AND l.loan_date::timestamptz < '2025-06-30'
    AND mt.name IN (SELECT name FROM keep_materials)
    AND l.renewal_count IS NULL
)
SELECT
  SUM(CASE
    WHEN campus_at_co IN (
      '7d02e46d-3e60-4eaf-a986-5aa3550e8cb5',
      'b23a14ae-b3a8-4cbf-92fb-4b81d1a4b0a1'
    )
    AND COALESCE(co_sp, '') NOT IN (SELECT id FROM smith_sp)
    AND co_sp IS NOT NULL
    THEN 1 ELSE 0
  END) AS consortial_lending_out
FROM base;

examples.question: Show me Smith College physical circulation at Smith, consortial lending out, and consortial borrowing in for FY 2024-2025 (July 1 to June 30)
examples.sql:
WITH smith_sp AS (
  SELECT unnest(array[
    '2c0764b7-63b3-4254-9950-0c730b7e438b',
    '6b6b9f00-aac7-4e20-a819-fb24386e48bb',
    '25d98f21-ef4d-4846-955e-17840062b1f0',
    '602aba21-73ae-4e43-a92e-91f2dee34c8f',
    '9e4b06c8-0cb0-4011-ab1d-a23af57d190c'
  ])::text AS id
),
keep_materials AS (
  SELECT unnest(array[
    'Book','Journal','Serial','Newspaper','Score',
    'Thesis/Dissertation','Government Publication','Microform',
    'DVD/Blu-ray','Audio CD','CD-ROM','Videocassette',
    'LP Phonorecord','Audiocassette','Film'
  ]) AS name
),
base AS (
  SELECT l.id, l.loan_date::timestamptz AS loan_dt,
    l.checkout_service_point_id AS co_sp,
    l.checkin_service_point_id AS ci_sp,
    loc.campus_id AS campus_at_co, mt.name AS mtype
  FROM circulation.loan__t l
  JOIN inventory.location__t loc ON loc.id = l.item_effective_location_id_at_check_out
  JOIN inventory.item__t it ON it.id = l.item_id
  JOIN inventory.material_type__t mt ON mt.id = it.material_type_id
  WHERE l.loan_date::timestamptz >= '2024-07-01'
    AND l.loan_date::timestamptz < '2025-06-30'
    AND mt.name IN (SELECT name FROM keep_materials)
    AND l.renewal_count IS NULL
)
SELECT
  SUM(CASE
    WHEN campus_at_co IN ('7d02e46d-3e60-4eaf-a986-5aa3550e8cb5','b23a14ae-b3a8-4cbf-92fb-4b81d1a4b0a1')
    AND co_sp IN (SELECT id FROM smith_sp)
    AND (ci_sp IS NULL OR ci_sp IN (SELECT id FROM smith_sp))
    THEN 1 ELSE 0
  END) AS physical_circ_at_smith,
  SUM(CASE
    WHEN campus_at_co IN ('7d02e46d-3e60-4eaf-a986-5aa3550e8cb5','b23a14ae-b3a8-4cbf-92fb-4b81d1a4b0a1')
    AND COALESCE(co_sp, '') NOT IN (SELECT id FROM smith_sp)
    AND co_sp IS NOT NULL
    THEN 1 ELSE 0
  END) AS consortial_lending_out,
  SUM(CASE
    WHEN campus_at_co NOT IN ('7d02e46d-3e60-4eaf-a986-5aa3550e8cb5','b23a14ae-b3a8-4cbf-92fb-4b81d1a4b0a1')
    AND co_sp IN (SELECT id FROM smith_sp)
    THEN 1 ELSE 0
  END) AS consortial_borrowing_in
FROM base;

examples.question: I want to see the entire library budget at Smith College. I want to look across multiple years from 2022 to current.
examples.sql:
SELECT 
            fyt."name" AS fiscal_year, 
            SUM(bt.allocated) AS total_allocated
        FROM 
            ldplite.finance.budget__t bt 
        INNER JOIN 
            ldplite.finance.fund__t ft ON bt.fund_id = ft.id
        INNER JOIN 
            ldplite.finance.fiscal_year__t fyt ON bt.fiscal_year_id = fyt.id
        WHERE 
            fyt.series = 'SCFY'
        GROUP BY 
            fyt."name"
        ORDER BY 
            fyt."name"

examples.question: How many items were created this year?
examples.sql:
WITH academic_year_dates AS (
    SELECT
        CASE
            WHEN CURRENT_DATE >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE) + INTERVAL '6 months'
            THEN date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE) + INTERVAL '6 months'
            ELSE date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE) - INTERVAL '6 months'
        END AS start_date,
        CASE
            WHEN CURRENT_DATE >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE) + INTERVAL '6 months'
            THEN date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE) + INTERVAL '1 year' + INTERVAL '6 months' - INTERVAL '1 day'
            ELSE date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE) + INTERVAL '6 months' - INTERVAL '1 day'
        END AS end_date
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS items_created
FROM inventory.item__t i, academic_year_dates a
WHERE i.metadata__created_date >= a.start_date
AND i.metadata__created_date <= a.end_date

examples.question: Show the highest circulating books at Neilson Library with total circulation
examples.sql:
WITH target_items AS (
    SELECT ii.id AS item_id, ii.hrid, ii.barcode,
           ii.effective_call_number_components__call_number AS call_number,
           inst.title AS instance_title
    FROM inventory.item__t ii
    JOIN inventory.holdings_record__t hr ON ii.holdings_record_id = hr.id
    JOIN inventory.instance__t inst ON hr.instance_id = inst.id
    JOIN inventory.material_type__t imt ON ii.material_type_id = imt.id
    JOIN inventory.location__t loc ON ii.effective_location_id = loc.id
    JOIN inventory.loclibrary__t lib ON loc.library_id = lib.id
    WHERE lib.name ILIKE '%Neilson%'
      AND LOWER(imt.name) = 'book'
),
current_circ AS (
    SELECT cl.item_id,
           COUNT(*) AS current_circulation,
           MAX(cl.loan_date) AS last_circulation_date
    FROM circulation.loan__t cl
    JOIN target_items ti ON cl.item_id = ti.item_id
    WHERE cl.action IN ('checkedout', 'checkedOutThroughOverride')
    GROUP BY cl.item_id
),
former_circ AS (
    SELECT itn.hrid,
           CAST(COALESCE(NULLIF(REGEXP_REPLACE(itn.notes__note, '\D', '', 'g'), ''), '0') AS INTEGER) AS former_circulation
    FROM inventory.item__t__notes itn
    JOIN target_items ti ON itn.hrid = ti.hrid
    WHERE itn.notes__item_note_type_id = 'f765f19f-9f1c-4688-8c79-ec366a730842'
)
SELECT
    ti.instance_title,
    ti.barcode AS item_barcode,
    ti.call_number,
    COALESCE(cc.current_circulation, 0) AS current_circulation,
    COALESCE(fc.former_circulation, 0) AS former_circulation,
    COALESCE(cc.current_circulation, 0) + COALESCE(fc.former_circulation, 0) AS total_circulation,
    cc.last_circulation_date
FROM target_items ti
LEFT JOIN current_circ cc ON ti.item_id = cc.item_id
LEFT JOIN former_circ fc ON ti.hrid = fc.hrid
ORDER BY total_circulation DESC
LIMIT 20

current_circ AS (
    SELECT al.loan__item_id AS item_id,
           COUNT(*) AS current_circulation,
           MAX(al.loan__loan_date) AS last_circulation_date
    FROM circulation.audit_loan__t al
    JOIN target_items ti ON al.loan__item_id = ti.item_id
    WHERE al.loan__action IN ('checkedout', 'checkedOutThroughOverride')
    GROUP BY al.loan__item_id
),
former_circ AS (
    SELECT itn.hrid,
           CAST(COALESCE(NULLIF(REGEXP_REPLACE(itn.notes__note, '\D', '', 'g'), ''), '0') AS INTEGER) AS former_circulation
    FROM inventory.item__t__notes itn
    JOIN target_items ti ON itn.hrid = ti.hrid
    WHERE itn.notes__item_note_type_id = 'f765f19f-9f1c-4688-8c79-ec366a730842'
)
SELECT
    ti.instance_title,
    ti.barcode AS item_barcode,
    ti.call_number,
    ti.material_type,
    ti.location_name,
    COALESCE(cc.current_circulation, 0) AS current_circulation,
    COALESCE(fc.former_circulation, 0) AS former_circulation,
    COALESCE(cc.current_circulation, 0) + COALESCE(fc.former_circulation, 0) AS total_circulation,
    cc.last_circulation_date
FROM target_items ti
LEFT JOIN current_circ cc ON ti.item_id = cc.item_id
LEFT JOIN former_circ fc ON ti.hrid = fc.hrid
ORDER BY total_circulation DESC
LIMIT 100

examples.question: How many items were created this year?
examples.sql:
WITH academic_year_dates AS (
    SELECT
        CASE
            WHEN CURRENT_DATE >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE) + INTERVAL '6 months'
            THEN date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE) + INTERVAL '6 months'
            ELSE date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE) - INTERVAL '6 months'
        END AS start_date,
        CASE
            WHEN CURRENT_DATE >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE) + INTERVAL '6 months'
            THEN date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE) + INTERVAL '1 year' + INTERVAL '6 months' - INTERVAL '1 day'
            ELSE date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE) + INTERVAL '6 months' - INTERVAL '1 day'
        END AS end_date
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS items_created
FROM inventory.item__t i, academic_year_dates a
WHERE i.metadata__created_date >= a.start_date
AND i.metadata__created_date <= a.end_date

examples.question: 100 Smith items that do not have a 300 field in their MARC record
examples.sql:
SELECT
    ii.hrid AS item_hrid,
    ii.barcode,
    inst.title AS instance_title,
    SUBSTRING(fsr.parsed_record__content FROM 1 FOR 200) AS marc_snippet
FROM inventory.item__t AS ii
JOIN inventory.holdings_record__t AS hr ON ii.holdings_record_id = hr.id
JOIN inventory.instance__t AS inst ON hr.instance_id = inst.id
JOIN folio_source_record.records__t AS fsr ON inst.id = fsr.external_ids_holder__instance_id
JOIN inventory.location__t AS loc ON ii.effective_location_id = loc.id
JOIN inventory.loclibrary__t AS lib ON loc.library_id = lib.id
JOIN inventory.loccampus__t AS camp ON lib.campus_id = camp.id
WHERE LOWER(camp.name) = LOWER('Smith College')
    AND fsr.parsed_record__content NOT ILIKE '%"300"%'
LIMIT 100;

examples.question: Smith College instances with material type Book that are missing MARC field 300
examples.sql:
WITH sc_book_instances AS MATERIALIZED (
    SELECT inst.id, inst.hrid, inst.title
    FROM inventory.instance__t inst
    WHERE EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
        FROM inventory.holdings_record__t hr
        JOIN inventory.location__t loc ON loc.id = hr.permanent_location_id
        JOIN inventory.loclibrary__t lib ON lib.id = loc.library_id
        JOIN inventory.loccampus__t camp ON camp.id = lib.campus_id
        WHERE hr.instance_id = inst.id
          AND camp.code = 'SC'
          AND EXISTS (
              SELECT 1
              FROM inventory.item__t ii
              WHERE ii.holdings_record_id = hr.id
                AND ii.material_type_id = (
                    SELECT id FROM inventory.material_type__t
                    WHERE LOWER(name) = 'book' LIMIT 1
                )
          )
    )
)
SELECT sbi.hrid, sbi.title
FROM sc_book_instances sbi
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM marctab.mt300 m
    WHERE m.instance_hrid = sbi.hrid
)
LIMIT 100
